exposure: Delivery mode (elective caesarean, emergency caesarean, assisted vaginal, spontaneous vaginal)
outcome: Cord blood high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) concentration
cohort: 934 singleton newborns and their mothers recruited from the University Medical Center Ulm, Southern Germany, between April 2012 and May 2013
finding: Cord blood leptin and hs-CRP concentrations were associated with duration of labour, but not mode of delivery, after adjusting for potential confounders.
mod_finding: While active labour modes were initially associated with higher leptin and hs-CRP, this association disappeared after adjusting for duration of labour.
